{"id": "6c3af3b2-db03-4def-9733-441146d7df5d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "BGP directions for Direct Connect VIF failover audit"}]}

{"id": "788b165e-5328-47bd-a053-58e208f06004", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Direct Connect failover resilience audits center on BGP session health in **both directions**, and both matter for different reasons:

**1. Inbound (from the Direct Connect / AWS side to your router)**
- Confirms AWS is actually advertising routes to you over each VIF.
- If this session is down or not advertising expected prefixes, you lose visibility into AWS-side reachability — even if the physical link looks healthy, you may have a silent routing black hole.

**2. Outbound (from your router to AWS)**
- Confirms your on-premises/CPE side is advertising your routes to AWS.
- If this fails, AWS can't route return traffic back to you, even though your inbound session looks fine — this is a classic asymmetric-failure trap in redundant VIF setups.

**Why check both, specifically for redundant VIFs:**
- A VIF can appear "up" at the BGP session level while only one direction is actually exchanging routes — this is the exact failure mode that defeats failover, because traffic gets black-holed on one leg instead of cleanly shifting to the healthy VIF.
- For true failover resilience, each redundant VIF needs to independently pass both direction checks — otherwise a "backup" path isn't really a backup; it just looks like one until you need it.
- You also want to verify route counts/prefixes match expectations in each direction (not just session state = "Up"), since a session can be established but advertising zero or partial routes.

Want me to pull up the actual VIF/BGP status for a specific Direct Connect connection in this account to check this live?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
